Swiss startup ClearSpace will oversee rendezvous and proximity operations, capture of the mission’s new debris target, ESA’s Project for On-Board Autonomy-1 (Proba-1) satellite and reentry in Earth’s atmosphere. Launch data has not yet been announced.

The 300-kilogram APS-R spacecraft is scheduled to launch in the summer of 2026 and will go to GEO, where it will approach a Space Force spacecraft. After fueling Tetra-5, APS-R will undock and move a safe distance away, then use a hyperspectral sensor to observe Tetra-5 for a leak check. APS-R will go to an Orbit Fab depot to refuel itself, then travel to a second, unidentified spacecraft for another refueling operation. In April 2025, USSF Space Systems Command (SSC) announced that Northrop Grumman has been contracted for two separate experiments for the Astroscale planned operation.
